reconciliation.reason: Later local work closed the frozen-auth publication and same-manager catalog/client subdomain. The original R6 deferral is narrowed rather than erased because automatic auth-change invalidation, centralized immutable runtime publication, and startup registration remain absent.

absorptions.upstream_title: Refresh MCP runtimes when session auth changes (#35146)
absorptions.semantic_mapping: Each local MCP rebuild captures one frozen auth snapshot and revision, constructs the replacement against that snapshot, and rechecks the auth generation under the publication guard before publishing. A stale auth generation is rejected. The published manager carries its auth binding, and advertised MCP tools retain a read guard on the exact manager generation used for dispatch, preventing a catalog from executing through a later client generation.
non_claims: No centralized immutable McpRuntime or ArcSwap publication model is claimed.
Authentication changes do not yet invalidate every loaded and still-starting runtime automatically.
No cross-account startup-race or plugin auth-mode parity claim is made.

deferrals.upstream_title: Prewarm MCP runtime updates in the background (#35144)
deferrals.reason: The local tree now has serialized desired/applied refresh generations and auth-bound publication, but it still lacks a published immutable McpRuntime plus a joined coalescing worker that rebuilds from the latest desired configuration and environment snapshot without allowing stale background work to publish.
missing_prerequisites: coalescing worker whose stale generations cannot publish
non_claims: No background MCP runtime publication or coalescing writer is absorbed.
The synchronous generation-bound refresh path is not evidence of background prewarm parity.

deferrals.upstream_title: Refresh MCP runtimes when session auth changes (#35146)
deferrals.reason: The local implementation now freezes and rechecks auth generation before publication and binds exposed tools to the executing manager generation. It still does not automatically invalidate every loaded and still-starting MCP runtime when authentication changes, publish one centralized immutable runtime projection, or prove startup and cross-account transitions end to end.
missing_prerequisites: automatic authentication-change invalidation trigger for loaded and starting runtimes
startup and cross-account transition regression proof
required_behavioral_tests: An old-generation runtime is revoked and cannot expose or execute tools after authentication rotation.
A real MCP Authorization header uses the new credential generation after rotation.
A cross-account transition cannot leak the prior account's tool catalog.
A startup authentication race cannot publish a mixed-credential runtime.
Tool exposure and execution always resolve through the same published generation.
non_claims: Frozen-auth publication does not imply automatic runtime refresh on every auth change.
Same-manager catalog dispatch does not close the still-starting runtime invalidation window.
